# **Shared Component Library Audit**

Audit of UI components that are candidates for a shared component library across the three extensions in the mono-repo: **AI Tutor**, **QuestionMaker**, and **EduAI Student Portal**. Based on screenshots of the AI Tutor implementation and wireframes for QuestionMaker and EduAI. Visual styling decisions (colours, light/dark mode) are addressed at the token level only — structure, behaviour, and accessibility requirements are the primary concern of this document.

### Resources:

[https://brand.ubc.ca/guidelines/downloads/ubc-colour-and-fonts/](https://brand.ubc.ca/guidelines/downloads/ubc-colour-and-fonts/)

## **1\. General Information**

### **1.1 Scope**

Three extensions share this mono-repo. Each has its own user-facing surface:

| Extension | Primary Users |
| ----- | ----- |
| **AI Tutor** | Students (lesson-taking), Instructors (course authoring), Admins (settings) |
| **QuestionMaker** | Instructors (question bank, assessment builder) |
| **EduAI Student Portal** | Students (courses, chat, AI tutor access) |

---

## **2\. Foundation: Tailwind CSS**

Tailwind CSS is a strong foundation for the shared component library. The majority of the low-level design decisions this document would otherwise need to prescribe from scratch — the spacing scale, the typographic scale, the colour system, border radii, focus ring utilities, dark mode toggling, and reduced motion handling — are already built into Tailwind and configurable via a single tailwind.config.js file.

Rather than maintaining a parallel set of CSS custom properties, the shared library should:

* Use **Tailwind's built-in utilities** for all spacing, sizing, typography, and layout.  
* Extend Tailwind's **theme** with UBC brand tokens (colours, fonts) so that bg-ubc-blue and text-ubc-gold work as first-class utilities throughout all extensions.  
* Use Tailwind's **darkMode: 'class'** strategy to enable the planned light/dark toggle — a .dark class on the root \<html\> element swaps all dark: prefixed utilities automatically.  
* Use Tailwind's **motion-reduce:** prefix for animations instead of a manual media query block.  
* Build components as React (or framework-equivalent) components that apply Tailwind classes internally and expose a clean, typed prop API externally.

The one area Tailwind does not address is semantic HTML and ARIA — those are covered in Section 6.5 and are non-negotiable regardless of the CSS framework in use.

## **3\. Design Tokens & UBC Brand**

### **3.1 Colour Palette**

UBC's official digital palette, to be added to tailwind.config.js as extended colours:

| Token name | Hex | Primary use |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| ubc-blue | \#002145 | Primary brand surface — nav backgrounds, primary button fill |
| ubc-gold | \#FFD100 | Accent — active indicators, highlights; **not for text on white** |
| ubc-light-blue | \#0055B3 | Interactive elements — links, focus rings |
| ubc-grey-dark | \#333333 | Body text |
| ubc-grey-light | \#F2F2F2 | Secondary surfaces, input backgrounds |

**Critical constraint:** UBC Gold (\#FFD100) fails WCAG contrast thresholds against white in both directions (ratio ≈ 1.1:1). It must only be used as a decorative fill or background with UBC Blue text on top. It cannot be used as a text colour on white, or have white text placed on it. See Section 6.2 for the full contrast table.

**Accent colour decision required:** The current AI Tutor implementation uses an amber-orange accent that is not UBC Gold. This needs to be resolved before the shared library is built — whether the accent aligns to UBC Gold, remains as a product-specific extended colour, or is replaced is a design decision that directly determines what the primary button background token resolves to.

### **3.2 Typography**

UBC's official typefaces are **Whitney** (sans-serif) and **Guardian Egyptian** (serif). Both are licensed — licence packages are available to UBC faculties and units via the brand site's font request form. They must not be committed to the repository as raw font files without confirming the appropriate delivery mechanism with the UBC brand team. Alternatives to these are **Open Sans** and **Arial**.

Configure both in tailwind.config.js so that font-sans and font-serif resolve to them across all extensions automatically, with a web-safe fallback stack for pre-load states.

Tailwind's built-in type scale (text-xs through text-3xl) maps cleanly to the scale this platform needs:

| Tailwind class | Size | Use |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| text-xs | 12px | Badge labels, timestamps, helper text |
| text-sm | 14px | Secondary labels, metadata |
| text-base | 16px | Body copy, input text, button labels |
| text-lg | 20px (default) | Card titles, minor headings |
| text-xl | 24px | Sub-page headings (\<h2\>) |
| text-2xl | 30px (default) | Page titles (\<h1\>) |
| text-3xl | 36px | Display headings (landing pages) |

No custom scale is needed — Tailwind's defaults are sufficient. The minimum text size anywhere in the UI is text-xs (12px). Do not render text below this size.

### **3.3 Spacing & Radius**

Tailwind's default spacing scale is base-4 (1 unit \= 4px). This is the standard — do not define a parallel custom scale. Use Tailwind's spacing tokens directly:

| Tailwind token | Value | Common use |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| p-3 | 12px | Input vertical padding |
| p-4 | 16px | Button horizontal padding, card internal padding |
| p-6 | 24px | Large card padding, modal padding |
| gap-4 | 16px | Minimum gap between cards in a grid |
| h-11 | 44px | Minimum touch target height — applied to all interactive elements |

For border radius, extend tailwind.config.js with named values that match the visual language:

| Token | Value | Use |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| rounded (default, 4px) | 4px | Small elements (tags, badges) |
| rounded-md (default, 6px) | 6px | Inputs, small cards |
| rounded-lg (default, 8px) | 8px | Cards, modals |
| rounded-full (default, 9999px) | pill | Status badges, avatar chips |

### **3.4 tailwind.config.js**

The shared tailwind.config.js lives in packages/ui and is extended by each app's own config. The following is the minimum required configuration:

```
// packages/ui/tailwind.config.js  
module.exports \= {  
  darkMode: 'class', // .dark on \<html\> drives the toggle across all extensions  
  theme: {  
    extend: {  
      colors: {  
        'ubc-blue':       '\#002145’,  
        'ubc-gold':       '\#FFD100',  
        'ubc-light-blue': '\#0055B3',  
        'ubc-grey-dark':  '\#333333',  
        'ubc-grey-light': '\#F2F2F2',  
      },  
      fontFamily: {  
        sans:  \['Whitney', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'sans-serif'\],  
        serif: \['Guardian Egyptian', 'Georgia', 'serif'\],  
      },  
      ringWidth: {  
        '3': '3px', // Tailwind's default stops at ring-4; ring-3 is the focus standard here  
      },  
      minHeight: {  
        'touch': '44px', // Named token for touch target floor  
      },  
    },  
  },  
}
```

Each app extends this:

```
// apps/ai-tutor/tailwind.config.js  
const base \= require('../../packages/ui/tailwind.config');

module.exports \= {  
  ...base,  
  content: \['./src/\*\*/\*.{ts,tsx}', '../../packages/ui/src/\*\*/\*.{ts,tsx}'\],  
};
```

## **4\. Shared Component Inventory**

### **4.1 Top Navigation Bar**

All three extensions use a persistent horizontal top bar with the same structural slots:

* **Left:** collapse toggle \+ product logo/branding  
* **Centre:** context-aware content — course picker dropdown (QuestionMaker, EduAI Portal) or text navigation links (AI Tutor)  
* **Right:** app-switcher badge, user name \+ role, utility links (Report Bug, Sign out)

The centre slot varies per extension but the surrounding shell is identical, making this a strong candidate for a shared component with an injected centre slot.

**![][image1]**

**Accessibility:** All right-side utility items must meet the 44×44px touch target minimum. Use min-h-touch flex items-center px-3 on each nav item. The hamburger toggle needs aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing to the nav region it opens. See Section 6.1.

**Proposed component:** `<TopNav brand, centreSlot, rightSlot />`

---

### **4.2 Sidebar Navigation**

The hamburger button in the top nav opens a collapsible sidebar panel containing the primary navigation for each extension. The panel structure is consistent across all three extensions:

* Top: product branding (logo \+ name)  
* Middle: vertical list of nav items, each with an icon and a text label, one of which carries an active/selected state at any given time  
* Bottom: utility links — Settings, Logout, and in AI Tutor a cross-app link back to EduAI

The EduAI Student Portal wireframes show: Dashboard, My Courses, Chat, AI Tutor (external). QuestionMaker shows: Questions, Assessments, Variants. The structure is identical; only the items differ per extension, making the sidebar shell a clear shared component with injected nav items.

The sidebar is independent of the top nav component — `<TopNav>` holds the hamburger trigger, `<SideNav>` is the panel itself. The two communicate via a shared open/close state managed at the layout level.

**Accessibility:** The hamburger trigger button must carry aria-expanded="true/false" and aria-controls pointing to the sidebar panel's id. The sidebar panel itself must be a `<nav aria-label="Site navigation">` landmark. When the sidebar opens, focus should move to the first nav item inside it. When it closes — whether by selecting an item, pressing Escape, or clicking the backdrop — focus must return to the hamburger button. On mobile, an overlay/backdrop behind the open sidebar must be dismissible by click or tap and must not trap focus behind it.

Nav items that are links use `<a href>`. The active item carries aria-current="page". If any nav item is icon-only at narrow widths (label hidden), it needs an aria-label.

**Proposed component:** `<SideNav items[], bottomItems[], isOpen, onClose />`

### **4.3 Breadcrumb (Page Pathing?)**

A slash-separated path of links ending in a plain-text current-page label appears across AI Tutor at multiple depth levels (Teaching \> CS101 \> Test 123 \> Lesson 1\) and in QuestionMaker's Assessment Builder. The pattern is identical.

![][image2]

**Accessibility:** Wrap in `<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">`. The final item carries aria-current="page" and must not be a link. Each link needs py-3 (padding-block: 12px) to reach 44px of tappable height. See Section 6.5.

**Proposed component:** `<Breadcrumb items[{ label, href }] />`

---

### **4.4 Page Header**

A large display title, optional subtitle or count badge, and right-aligned action buttons appear at the top of every primary page across all three extensions. The badge slot (e.g. "1 COURSE", "FROM .ENV") keeps count and environment indicators out of the header component's logic.

**Proposed component:** `<PageHeader title, subtitle, badge, actions />`

---

### **4.5 Button**

The same button vocabulary appears in all three extensions. Five variants observed:

| Variant | Description | Examples | Image |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| primary | Filled, high-contrast label | Add Module, Save, Sign in with EduAI, Submit Answer  | ![][image3]![][image4] |
| secondary | Outlined | Import, Cancel, Reset changes, Preview | ![][image5]![][image6] |
| ghost | No border, text-only | View course, Prev/Next, Clear All | ![][image7] |
| icon | No label, icon only | Card arrow (→), Send, Hamburger | ![][image8] |
| ai | Primary with sparkle icon prefix | Guide me, Take Tour, Generate | ![][image9]![][image10] |

**Accessibility:** Icon-only buttons must have aria-label. Decorative icons inside buttons must have aria-hidden="true". All buttons must meet the 44px height floor. See Sections 6.1 and 6.5.

**Proposed component:** `<Button variant, sizeX, sizeY, icon, iconPosition, ariaLabel, disabled, loading />`

### **4.6 Badges & Status Chips**

A consistent pill-shaped badge vocabulary appears across all three extensions. One base component with a variant prop covers all cases.

| Category | Values observed | Examples |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Status** | Published, Reviewed, Active, Completed, Draft, Unhandled | ![][image11]![][image12]![][image13]![][image14]![][image15] |
| **Role** | STUDENT, ADMIN, PROFESSOR |  |
| **Difficulty** | Easy, Medium, Hard  | ![][image16] |
| **Question format** | MCQ, Short Answer, Long Answer | ![][image17] |
| **Content hierarchy** | MODULE, LESSON, QUESTION |  |
| **Source** | EDUAI, AI, GOOGLE, OPENAI | ![][image18] |
| **Tier / cost** | LOW COST, BALANCED COST, TUTOR DEFAULT, SUPERVISOR DEFAULT |  |
| **Count** | 1 COURSE, 1 MODULE, 48 questions | ![][image19] |

**Accessibility:** Badges conveying meaningful state (role, status) must be included in the accessible name of their parent row or linked via aria-describedby. See Section 6.5.

**Proposed components:**

* \<Badge variant, label /\> — base pill  
* \<Tag label, onRemove? /\> — topic chip; removable in forms, read-only in cards  
* \<TagInput value\[\], onChange, suggestions? /\> — multi-tag input

### **4.7 Form Controls**

The same form primitives appear across all three extensions, currently implemented independently. All require a shared baseline covering: \<label\> association, hint text, error state, disabled state, and focus ring.

| Control | Where observed |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Text input** | New module/lesson title, API key, button title with char counter, search bars |
| **Textarea** | Custom AI prompt, question content, chat input |
| **Select / Dropdown** | Main topic, model selection, difficulty |
| **Checkbox** | AI Study Buddy Modes, model enable/disable, test checklists |
| **Toggle / Switch** | Enable dual loop (Admin), Finalized (QuestionMaker) |
| **Segmented control** | MCQ / Short answer switcher, Teach me / Guide me mode, Settings tabs, difficulty selector |
| **Number input** | Max revision passes (Admin) |

**Accessibility:** Missing labels on inline inputs, undersized checkbox tap targets, and incorrect role on toggles are the primary issues. See Sections 6.1 and 6.5.

**Proposed components:** `<Input />`, `<Textarea />`, `<Select />`,`<Checkbox />`, `<Toggle />`, `<SegmentedControl />` — all sharing a common prop interface: label, hint, error, disabled, required.

### **4.8 Card**

A rounded container with an icon or index, title, metadata, status, and footer area appears across all three extensions in multiple contexts:

* Instructor course cards (Teaching view)  
* Instructor module and lesson cards  
* Student course, module, and lesson cards  
* Question cards (QuestionMaker)  
* Assessment cards (QuestionMaker)  
* Course cards (EduAI Portal)

These share enough structure — header, body, footer slots — that a base \<Card\> with composable slots covers all cases. The numbered index circle (01, 02...) is a reusable sub-component.

**Proposed components:**

* `<Card header, body, footer />`  
* `<IndexBadge number />` — the numbered circle in module/lesson cards

---

### **4.9 Stat Grid**

A small grid of labelled values appears inside cards across multiple extensions: question count \+ sections on assessment cards, overall progress \+ current module on course cards. The structure (label above, value below, columns) is identical.

**Proposed component:** `<StatGrid items[{ label, value }] />`

---

### **4.10 Modal**

A centred overlay with a title or icon, body content, and a Cancel \+ primary action footer appears in both AI Tutor (knowledge level selection) and QuestionMaker (Create/Edit Question, Question History). The shell is identical.

The knowledge level modal introduces a **card option selector**: three side-by-side cards (Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced) acting as a mutually exclusive choice. This sub-pattern is broadly reusable wherever a radio group benefits from more visual space than a dropdown allows.

![][image20]

**Accessibility:** Focus must move into the modal on open, be trapped inside it, and return to the trigger on close. The card option selector must use `<fieldset> + <input type="radio">` semantics — not `<div>` click handlers. See Section 6.5.

**Proposed components:**

* `<Modal title, icon, onClose, footer />`
* `<ModalFooter cancelLabel, confirmLabel, onCancel, onConfirm, isLoading />`  
* `<CardOptionGroup name, options\[{ value, label, description }\], value, onChange />`

---

### **4.11 Data Table**

The Admin Bug Reports view renders a sortable table with typed column content and inline row actions (status dropdown, Copy / Console / Network / Screenshot buttons). The component is currently the only table in the UI but the pattern is broadly reusable in any admin or list view.

**Accessibility:** Must use `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<th scope="col">` markup. Sortable columns need aria-sort. Inline controls per row need accessible names that include row context. See Section 6.5.

**Proposed component:** `<DataTable columns[], rows[], onSort />`

---

### **4.12 App Switcher Badge**

The green pill displaying "EduAI" in the AI Tutor top nav and the "AI Service Online" indicator in QuestionMaker are the same component: a live status badge showing whether the EduAI AI service is reachable. It is not a navigation element. Its presence in both extensions makes it a clear shared component.

The badge has at least two states — online (green) and unavailable (visible in QuestionMaker's Create Question modal where it renders as "AI Service Unavailable" with a warning treatment). A third degraded/connecting state is likely needed in practice.

**Accessibility:** Status must not be communicated through colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The text label ("AI Service Online", "AI Service Unavailable") already satisfies this, but the label must never be dropped in favour of a colour-only dot. If the badge includes a refresh/retry icon button, that button needs an aria-label ("Retry AI service connection"). Status changes that happen after page load should be announced via an aria-live=”polite” region so screen reader users are informed without being interrupted.

**Proposed component:** ` <AIServiceStatus /> — statuses: "online", "unavailable", "connecting" `

---

### **4.13 Prompt Suggestions List**

In AI Tutor's "Guide me" state, clickable pre-set prompts appear as a list that populates the chat input. The same pattern appears in the EduAI Student Portal chat.

**Proposed component:** `<PromptSuggestions prompts[], onSelect />`

---

### **4.14 Alert & Callout**

Two informational display patterns appear across the extensions:

* **Alert:** System-level message with a colour-coded border — e.g. the data privacy warning in QuestionMaker's Create Question modal, or the "Before you save" block in Admin settings.  
* **Callout:** Inline highlighted block for surfacing key content — e.g. the "Key Takeaway" box in the EduAI chat.

One component with a variant prop (info, warning, error, success) covers both.

**Proposed component:** `<Alert variant, title, message />`

## **5\. Extension-Specific Components**

These components appear in one extension only and are too tightly coupled to that extension's domain model to be meaningfully abstracted. Their internal parts use shared primitives from Section 4; the assembled component is not a shared concern.

**AI Study Buddy Panel (AI Tutor — Student Lesson View)** The composite of setup flow (knowledge level, API key entry), mode tabs (Teach me / Guide me), prompt suggestions, and embedded chat input is specific to AI Tutor's pedagogical model. No equivalent exists in the other extensions. Its internal parts (SegmentedControl, PromptSuggestions, Button, Select) are all shared; the panel itself is not.

**Instructor Activity Editor (AI Tutor — Lesson Detail View)** The activity configuration panel — topic selectors, AI Study Buddy mode checkboxes, char-counted button title input, custom prompt textarea with placeholder syntax tips — is specific to AI Tutor's content authoring model.

**Admin Model Configuration (AI Tutor — EduAI Settings)** The model selection checklist — checkbox cards with provider badge, cost tier badge, default badges, description, and monospace model string — is specific to AI loop policy configuration. Abstracting it into a shared component would add coupling with no benefit to the other extensions.

**Landing Page Onboarding Animation (AI Tutor — Welcome Screen)** The animated node graph on the login page is a marketing surface specific to this extension.

## **6\. Implementation Specifications**

### **6.1 Touch Targets & Interactive Sizing**

**What to implement**

Every interactive element must have a tappable area of at least **44×44 CSS pixels**. Tailwind's h-11 (44px) and min-h-touch (custom token from Section 3.4) are the primary utilities. The visual size of the element does not need to be 44px — the hit area must be.

| Component | Approx. visual size | Fix |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Primary / secondary button | Varies | min-h-touch (44px) built into component default |
| Hamburger trigger button | \~24–32px | min-h-touch \+ p-2.5 built into \<TopNav\> |
| Sidebar nav items | \~36–40px tall typically | min-h-touch flex items-center px-4 on each \<a\> |
| Checkbox | \~16px box | min-h-touch flex items-center on the \<label\> wrapper |
| Toggle switch | \~24px tall | Same as checkbox — expand the label row |
| Segmented control tab | Varies | min-h-touch per tab built into component |
| Breadcrumb link | \~20px line height | py-3 (padding-block: 12px) on each \<a\> |
| Tag chip remove (×) | \~8px | ::after with absolute inset-\[-10px\] |
| Top nav utility links (Sign out, Report Bug) | \~20px text | py-2.5 px-3 on each item |

**Why**

WCAG 2.5.5 (Target Size, Level AA) sets 44×44px as the minimum. This platform serves students who may have motor impairments or use touch-based assistive technology. An undersized button that a mouse user clicks without issue is a real barrier for these users. Fixing touch targets in the shared component layer prevents the issue from recurring per extension.

**Consider**

WCAG 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, Level AA in WCAG 2.2) adds a secondary rule: if an element is smaller than 24×24px visually, adequate spacing must surround it to bring the offset area to 24px in each dimension. The 44px floor from 2.5.5 is more conservative and should be the target. Where layout permits, 48×48px (the Material Design and Apple HIG recommendation) improves usability for all users, not only those with impairments.

### **6.2 Colour & Contrast**

**What to implement**

All text must meet the following ratios against its background, measured using the WCAG relative luminance formula:

| Text type | Minimum ratio | Applies to |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Normal text (\< 24px regular or \< \~19px bold) | **4.5:1** | Body, labels, badge text, input text, button labels, links |
| Large text (≥ 24px regular or ≥ \~19px bold) | **3:1** | Page titles, display headings |
| UI components and graphical objects | **3:1** | Button borders, input borders, progress fill, toggle track, focus ring |

Verified ratios for the UBC palette:

| Foreground | Background | Ratio | Result |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| White \#FFFFFF | UBC Blue \#002145 | \~16.7:1 | ✅ Normal text |
| UBC Blue \#002145 | White \#FFFFFF | \~16.7:1 | ✅ Normal text |
| UBC Light Blue \#0055B3 | White \#FFFFFF | \~7.0:1 | ✅ Normal text |
| UBC Blue \#002145 | UBC Gold \#FFD100 | \~15.3:1 | ✅ Normal text |
| UBC Gold \#FFD100 | White \#FFFFFF | \~1.1:1 | ❌ Fails all thresholds |
| White \#FFFFFF | UBC Gold \#FFD100 | \~1.1:1 | ❌ Fails all thresholds |
| \#333333 | White \#FFFFFF | \~12.6:1 | ✅ Normal text |
| \#333333 | \#F2F2F2 | \~10.7:1 | ✅ Normal text |

**Why**

WCAG 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum, Level AA) mandates these ratios. The key finding: **UBC Gold cannot be used as a text colour on white, and white text cannot be placed on UBC Gold**. Both pairings fail at ≈1.1:1. UBC Gold is usable as a decorative fill, icon colour on dark backgrounds, or as a background with UBC Blue (\#002145) text on top.

**Consider**

Contrast must be verified for every interactive state, not just the default — hover, focus, disabled, and placeholder states all need independent checks. Placeholder text in inputs is commonly muted to the point of failure; \#767676 on white is the lightest grey that passes (4.54:1). Disabled controls are exempt from WCAG 1.4.3, but should remain readable where layout permits. For dark mode, every colour pair must be re-verified with its dark-mode resolved token values — a light-mode pass does not transfer.

---

### **6.3 Typography**

**What to implement**

Configure fonts in tailwind.config.js (see Section 3.4). Then apply Tailwind's type utilities directly — no custom scale is needed.

| Property | Tailwind utility | Notes |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Body font | font-sans | Resolves to Whitney via config |
| Display / heading font | font-serif | Resolves to Guardian Egyptian via config |
| Body size | text-base (16px) | Do not render body below this |
| Minimum text size | text-xs (12px) | Applies to badge labels and timestamps |
| Body line height | leading-relaxed (1.625) | Slightly more than WCAG's 1.5 minimum requirement |
| Heading line height | leading-tight (1.25) | Applied to all \<h1\> through \<h3\> |
| Heading weight | font-semibold or font-bold | Depends on heading level |

**Why**

WCAG 1.4.12 (Text Spacing, Level AA) requires that users can increase line height to 1.5× font size, letter spacing to 0.12× font size, and word spacing to 0.16× font size without loss of content. Using Tailwind's unitless leading-\* utilities and rem\-based font sizes (which scale with the user's browser preference setting) satisfies this automatically.

**Consider**

Whitney and Guardian Egyptian are licensed fonts. Confirm the appropriate delivery mechanism with the UBC brand team before serving them — committing raw font files to the repository may violate licence terms. Until fonts are confirmed, the fallback stacks defined in the Tailwind config ('Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif and Georgia, serif) apply automatically and maintain the correct font-family role for each context.

---

### **6.4 Focus Indicators**

**What to implement**

Every interactive element must show a visible focus ring on keyboard focus. Use Tailwind's focus-visible: prefix — this applies the ring for keyboard navigation only, not mouse clicks, so it is not visually intrusive for pointer users.

Standard ring applied to all interactive elements:
```
focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ubc-light-blue focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-none
```
* **Ring width:** ring-3 (3px) — ring-3 requires the custom ringWidth entry in the config from Section 3.4  
* **Ring colour:** ring-ubc-light-blue (\#0055B3) — 7:1 against white, passes both light and dark surface requirements on most backgrounds  
* **Offset:** ring-offset-2 (2px) — separates the ring from the element edge for clarity

For elements on dark surfaces or coloured card backgrounds (dark mode, coloured panels):
```
dark:focus-visible:ring-ubc-gold dark:focus-visible:ring-offset-ubc-blue
```
UBC Gold (\#FFD100) against UBC Blue (\#002145) achieves \~15:1, making it clearly visible on dark surfaces.
For elements that sit on mixed-colour backgrounds, a two-layer ring ensures visibility on any surface:
```
focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ubc-light-blue focus-visible:ring-offset-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-white
```
**Why**

WCAG 2.4.7 (Focus Visible, Level AA) requires a visible focus indicator. WCAG 2.4.11 (Focus Appearance, Level AA in WCAG 2.2) adds that the indicator must have a minimum area and 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours. Removing the browser default :focus outline with outline-none without adding a replacement makes the interface inaccessible to keyboard users. Using focus-visible: instead of focus: is the correct modern approach — it shows the ring for keyboard users while suppressing it for mouse users who find it distracting.

**Consider**

The focus-visible: prefix relies on the :focus-visible CSS pseudo-class, which has full support in all modern browsers but may need a polyfill for older targets. Define the ring utilities in the shared base component styles rather than relying on individual component authors to apply them correctly. A component that does not handle focus styling should fail code review.

---

### **6.5 Semantic HTML & ARIA**

**What to implement**

The following requirements are structural, not stylistic. Tailwind has no bearing on them.

| Component | Required semantics |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Page structure** | One \<h1\> per page. Section titles use \<h2\>. Card titles use \<h3\>. Never skip heading levels. |
| **Navigation regions** | Top nav in \<nav aria-label="Main"\>. Breadcrumb in \<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"\>. Multiple \<nav\> elements on one page must each have a distinct aria-label. |
| **Breadcrumb current page** | Last item carries aria-current="page" and is not a link. |
| **Buttons vs. links** | \<button\> for actions (submit, open modal, toggle state). \<a href\> for navigation. Never use \<div\> or \<span\> with a click handler as a substitute. |
| **Icon-only buttons** | aria-label naming the specific action in context. Decorative icons inside buttons: aria-hidden="true". |
| **Modals** | role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby pointing to the modal title id. Focus trap on open. Focus returns to trigger element on close. |
| **Progress bars** | role="progressbar", aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin="0", aria-valuemax. Associate label text via aria-label or aria-describedby. |
| **Toggle / switch** | role="switch", aria-checked="true/false". Not type="checkbox" — a toggle signals an immediate effect, a checkbox signals pending form state. |
| **Card option selectors** | \<fieldset\> \+ \<legend\> \+ \<input type="radio"\>. The Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced cards are a radio group styled visually as cards — they are not \<div\> elements. |
| **Checkboxes** | Native \<input type="checkbox"\> with an associated \<label\> via for/id. Custom implementations require explicit ARIA only if native styling is truly insufficient. |
| **Inputs without visible labels** | A visually hidden \<label\> (Tailwind's sr-only class) is required. Placeholder text alone is not a label substitute and must not be used as one. |
| **Sortable table headers** | \<table\>, \<thead\>, \<th scope="col"\>. Active sort column carries aria-sort="ascending" or "descending". Unsorted columns carry aria-sort="none". |
| **Inline row controls** | aria-label must include row context — "Change status for: Test 123 does not load," not just "Status." |
| **Status badges in list rows** | Badge text must be reachable via the row's accessible name or linked via aria-describedby. A screen reader should read "Sample Student, Student role, student@eduai.local" — not "Sample Student" with the role badge announced separately. |
| **App switcher** | aria-label="Switch to EduAI". Not just "EduAI." |

**Why**

Screen readers, keyboard navigation, and switch access devices all depend on semantic HTML to understand what they are interacting with. A \<div\> with a click handler is announced as "group" or nothing, is not reachable by Tab, does not respond to Enter or Space, and cannot communicate disabled or selected state. These are not cosmetic concerns — they determine whether the interface works at all for a portion of users. Given that accessible education is this platform's purpose, semantic correctness is load-bearing.

**Consider**

ARIA supplements HTML semantics — it does not replace them. A \<button\> does not need role="button". Reach for ARIA only when no native HTML element covers the pattern (e.g. role="dialog", role="progressbar", role="switch"). Overuse of ARIA on elements that already have correct semantics creates noise for screen reader users.

Dynamic content updates need aria-live regions. When the AI Study Buddy response streams in, when a module is marked complete, or when a filter updates the question list — screen reader users receive no notification unless the changing region carries aria-live="polite" (non-urgent updates) or aria-live="assertive" (urgent alerts). This must be planned into the chat and progress update components from the start, not retrofitted later.

---

### **6.6 Reduced Motion**

**What to implement**

Use Tailwind's motion-reduce: prefix on any utility that produces movement:

transition-all duration-200 motion-reduce:transition-none

animate-spin motion-reduce:animate-none 

For components where the animation is applied in JavaScript or cannot be expressed as a Tailwind utility (e.g. the AI Tutor landing page node graph), use the prefers-reduced-motion media query directly:
```
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {  
  .node-graph-animation {  
    animation: none;  
  }  
}
```
Apply a global safety net in the shared base stylesheet to catch anything missed at the component level:
```
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {  
  \*, \*::before, \*::after {  
    animation-duration: 0.01ms \!important;  
    transition-duration: 0.01ms \!important;  
    scroll-behavior: auto \!important;  
  }  
} 
```
**Why**

The prefers-reduced-motion OS setting is used by people with vestibular disorders, epilepsy, and motion sensitivity, for whom animation can cause disorientation or physical harm. WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, Level AAA) recommends disabling motion-based animation when the user has requested it. While AAA is not mandatory, this is a low-cost CSS change with meaningful benefit and has full browser support.

**Consider**

Reduced motion does not mean no transitions at all. Opacity fades (no movement) are generally acceptable even under prefers-reduced-motion. What must be suppressed are spatial transforms — anything involving an object moving across the screen. Instant state changes with no transition are also acceptable and are often a cleaner solution than fading.

### **Shared Components**

TopNav, SideBar, Breadcrumb, PageHeader, Button (5 variants), Badge, Tag, TagInput, Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Toggle, SegmentedControl, Card, IndexBadge, StatGrid, ProgressBar, Modal, ModalFooter, CardOptionGroup, DataTable, AppSwitcherBadge, PromptSuggestions, Alert

### **Extension-Specific Composites (Not Shared)**

AI Study Buddy panel, Instructor activity editor, Admin model configuration checklist, Landing page onboarding animation
